title: Personally Taught
text: “Come now, Wolf, you’re coming along as a witness too, indeed.”
“Kuun.”
Wolf was clinging to Father as if refusing to let go. How old are you again? Think about your age, it’s pathetic, I say. I could almost understand why Coward and Takt named you what they did.

“Um… Motoyasu-kun, there are quite a few days between here and Faubrey, right? Since you’ll be coming back this way at some point anyway, why don’t we handle Wolf’s side of things quietly through Siltvelt while you’re gone?”
Father proposed this to Wolf with a somewhat wry smile. Hmm… well, if Father says so, I suppose there’s no helping it.
“Understood. Well then, Wolf, once we arrive in Faubrey, you’ll come with me, indeed.”
“Vaf.”
Getting a response like that while in Demi-Human form was rather deflating. No offense to Father, but you really do suit a beastman form better, I say.
“Well then, let’s be off, Yuki-chan.”
“Yes sir!”

And so, we loaded Takt and his lot onto the carriage and made our way straight to Faubrey, indeed. Discreetly, of course. Under Yuki-chan’s direction, the Filolial-samas took turns pulling us along cheerfully. We arrived at Faubrey in no time at all. Naturally, I subjected Takt to torture along the way.

Spear Hero arrived in secret without delay, presenting the bound Takt before Pig King. Of course, I explained in detail how pathetically he’d lost at the Zeltoble colosseum. It seemed Takt still hadn’t given up, because even while paralyzed mid-explanation, he let out groans of protest. Ah, and the minister from Takt’s faction, who had initially been smirking under the assumption this was all some impostor’s doing, changed his expression completely the moment the stripping of status took effect right before his eyes—and in the very act of trying to defend Takt, he was promptly taken into custody as well. Pig King seemed quite satisfied with this unexpected turn of events, and secured a promise to fabricate a cover story while purging the pigs of Takt’s faction.

Wolf testified as witness to Takt’s misdeeds, in his capacity as one of the Seven Star Heroes on Siltvelt’s side. Father had wanted to come along too, but there was no need to trouble him with it. After Takt was fitted with a heavy-duty slave brand and made to watch the spectacle of Pig King toying with the pigs of that faction… it became my turn, indeed. By that point, Takt seemed to have grown tired of screaming and had the look of someone begging to be killed, but I couldn’t possibly finish him off at this level, I say. And so, I hauled Takt to the research facility on Nanareppa Island, strapped him to the test platform, and… administered a form of torture that had just occurred to me.
“Takt, how are you feeling right now, I wonder? You wished to become immortal, didn’t you?”
Thoroughly rotten reincarnators, it’s said, always crave the strongest form of immortality.
“—Aaaaahhh… Wooooh!”
“You don’t think mere groaning like that will earn you forgiveness, do you?”
I made full use of the alchemy skills available through my spear techniques, indeed.
“Look, Wolf, you should feel satisfied too, seeing Takt in such a pathetic state.”
“Kyaiin kyaiin!?”

Even though I was kindly showing Wolf Takt’s torture to help him feel better, he got scared and tried to run away. Later on, Wolf had apparently overwritten this whole memory with something else entirely. Yes—what I did to Takt this time around was combine Yggdrasil medicine with various life-force restoration effects… turning him into a living lump of flesh that couldn’t die so long as the medication lasted. This, indeed, is the Flesh Lump Punishment, personally taught by Ark! I was inspired to borrow the technique! Oh? In my memory, Ark seems to be wincing and saying “I’d really rather you not copy that too much…” but considering the countless Filolial-sama eggs Takt shattered, this is a fitting punishment, indeed.

At any rate, that’s how I dealt with Takt personally, indeed. He’ll go on living as an immobile lump of flesh unable to die, forever paying for his crime of desecrating Filolial-sama lives. Well, I did administer him a fitting punishment on that infamous island. Eventually, there’ll likely be a reincarnator battle royale, and he’d make a fine exhibit for that occasion. Incidentally, I later learned that Rival too had been given a similar punishment through magic. In any case, the grudge between Wolf and Takt had come to light, and thus it was resolved.

While I was still transporting Takt, during one of the Filolial-sama shift changes when I returned, I happened upon Father speaking with an envoy from Siltvelt. Elephant was there too, apparently in the middle of a lengthy discussion.
“To think Wolf was actually Magram-sama all along… Even I had no idea.”
“So it seems. Um, apparently Wolf made contact with the upper echelons of Siltvelt while keeping an eye out for anyone connected to Takt.”
Wolf wasn’t present at the time. It seemed he was off having various discussions in Siltvelt.
“Magram-sama, is it…”
“Was that someone you knew too, Elmelo-san?”

“Only from a distance, long ago, when Janon-sama was making rounds through various regions. I… caught a glimpse. It felt so different that I had the illusion of having met him somewhere before, but truthfully, I had no idea.”
It seemed Elephant had met him once, long ago. Somehow or other, Elephant really does know a lot of people.
“I see. Motoyasu-kun, you don’t know anything about Wolf at all, do you?”
“Not in the slightest, indeed.”
I’d never had the slightest interest, after all.
“Come to think of it, once Wolf regained himself, his appearance changed quite a bit. I wonder what kind of phenomenon that is?”
“Indeed. His transformed appearance changed considerably.”
Not only did his build grow larger, but even his coloring changed entirely.

“Magram-sama, much like Ruhabert-sama, is called a wolf-man in Melromarc, but in Siltvelt, he belongs to a lineage regarded as an ancient breed among the Warful species. According to one theory, his blood carries a demonic quality rivaling even that of dragons.”
“Demonic…”

“Yes. It’s said to be the species closest to what generations of heroes envision as vampires, yet distinct in its overflowing wildness. I myself am close to the Warful species, but the difference is so vast it’s almost frustrating.”
The Siltvelt envoy answered Father’s question with a somewhat wry smile.

“So, to answer Shield Hero-sama’s question: when Magram-sama transforms, he combines his own demonic nature with the surrounding power to become an even more powerful beastman form. Among dragons, there are those who change their attributes or appearance depending on the circumstances—I think it’s best understood as something close to that.”

Come to think of it, Rival had also changed her transformed appearance by coordinating with Assistant and Mole. Eventually she became able to change it freely on her own, so I suppose it was something along those lines. According to information later extracted from Takt’s remaining followers, the second-stage transformation of the pig who’d been serving as Shieldfreeden’s representative had apparently been developed using a factor discovered through human experimentation on Wolf. Couldn’t you achieve the same thing through a Limit Break Class Up without resorting to something like that? Well, knowing that pig of Takt’s, he probably lacked the necessary factor or the heart for it. More importantly, what I needed to be wary of was the fact that Wolf, like Rival, could apparently change his beastman form depending on the situation. …Was this perhaps something I ought to be on guard about? Ah, well, it’s probably fine.
“Father, I heard that Wolf went to Siltvelt while I was away transporting Takt. How did that go?”
